Adopt native Codex projections within Cassy authority

Use native lifecycle and role projections within Cassy's ownership; validate transport replacements before adoption. Confidence: high in the bounded structure, moderate in unmeasured adapter benefits.

Lifecycle and trust: adopt a bounded projection

The hook guide documents merged matching hooks across active configuration layers; a higher layer does not simply replace lower hooks. Project trust can exclude project layers while user/system hooks remain. Exact hook-definition trust and managed restrictions are separate controls. features.hooks=false, managed feature pins and managed-only hook policy must remain effective operator constraints; a supported feature does not authorize enabling it.

Tool matching covers shell aliases, file-edit aliases and MCP tool names, with stated opt-outs and hosted-tool limitations. A PreToolUse denial is useful only when the handler emits a supported decision. Unsupported/malformed output and some handler errors continue execution; MCP hook failures/timeouts are documented as fail-open. These mechanisms cannot be the only authority boundary. Auto-review failures have a different, fail-closed contract in the security guide; the two failure policies must not be conflated.

Executed peer evidence: cas-d0fe's immutable canary/results/20261017T211351Z/ANALYSIS.md, using codex-cli 0.163.0 with model gpt-6.1-sol, proves SessionStart ran and its developer context was consumed, and Bash/MCP-name PreToolUse matching fired before approval. MCP execution itself was refused by the canary's approval policy and remains unexercised. This task launched no model session.

The discriminating canary/results/stop-20261017T211715Z/ANALYSIS.md proves trusted Stop blocking caused continuation, a subsequent stop_hook_active=true stopped cleanly, and an untrusted UserPromptSubmit control stayed silent while a trusted hook ran. Its hooks/list receipt shows matcher-ignored events omit the matcher from trust identity; Cassy's existing helper always included an empty matcher. This resolves the earlier silent-Stop ambiguity. It does not reproduce every historical operator trust prompt.

At Cassy base, crates/cas-pty/src/codex_trust.rs pins older hash behavior, cas-cli/src/cli/hook/config_gen.rs generates tool hooks, and crates/cas-mux/src/backend/codex.rs:21 reports static hook support false. Adopt the adapter direction through cas-d0fe, preserving exact trust, existing user files and explicit disablement. Then verify installation/review and real failed/successful execution controls before claiming enforcement.

Async hooks are unsuitable for admission, policy or Stop continuation: the guide makes their output deferred to a safe model point, gives them no blocking/rewrite power and does not promise to wake an idle session. Keep blocking lifecycle paths synchronous and continuation bounded by the native re-entry field.

Roles, skills and independent verification

The subagent guide defines personal ~/.codex/agents/*.toml and project .codex/agents/*.toml, with name, description and developer_instructions. Canonical Cassy role bodies can generate these projections without duplicating policy. Preserve unowned files/symlinks and intentional operator overrides. Role configuration can override model/effort selection; inherited approval, sandbox and provider constraints cannot be strengthened merely by describing an agent as read-only.

At base, cas-cli/src/harness_policy.rs:231 derives required verification from static optional capability bits. hooks/handlers/handlers_events/pre_tool.rs:1016 and handlers_state.rs:645 bind a registered Task/Agent handoff to SubagentStart. A discoverable Codex role, spawn response or native turn is not that sealed registration. Adopt cas-6c54's contextual capability separation and independent-review fallback, subject to its implementation review. Never make independent review disappear because an optional native feature is unavailable; preserve explicitly authorized skip policy.

There is a concrete docs/stable-source discrepancy. The live guide describes agents.enabled=false as disabling multi-agent behavior. In 0.163.0 config resolution, enabled multi_agent_v2 selects V2 before checking that boolean. The pinned feature definitions distinguish V1 multi_agent (stable, default true) and V2 (stable, default false). Consequently one flag is insufficient effective-availability evidence. Record requested disablement and report a conflict/unknown where the native effective state is unresolved; do not silently rewrite settings.

The skill guide uses canonical .agents/skills discovery, including repository ancestors and personal scope. Equal names do not merge; agents/openai.yaml can disable implicit invocation while retaining explicit invocation. Dependencies metadata is not permission to install servers. Cassy currently shares legacy CODEX_HOME/skills; an app-server example also uses .codex/skills. Test discovery and duplicate/override behavior before migration, using owned projections rather than moving user content. Custom prompts are deprecated; cas-558a already owns the existing finish-skill/diary reconciliation, so this report requests no overlapping edit.

Native readers: preserve unknowns

Prefer supported native evidence over a second implementation of CLI/project/profile/managed precedence. The app-server reference documents config/read with cwd and includeLayers, and configRequirements/read for constraints. The latter spelling matters. They reveal layered on-disk configuration and origins, not a complete callable-tool list for an active model turn. Feature-list state similarly does not establish every model's tool availability.

Pinned schemas confirm the limit: ConfigReadParams supports cwd/layers; configuration permits additional fields; the fetched ModelProviderCapabilitiesReadResponse contains image-generation and web-search information, not an authoritative native-agent catalog.

The documented debug prompt-input is not a resolved-tools reader. In the stable CLI, it builds configuration and performs authentication/Git/skill setup; prompt_debug returns input messages (Vec<ResponseItem>). No invocation was made here. No complete supported resolved role/tool reader was found in the reviewed docs/source, so that field stays Unknown rather than guessed.

Recommended capability evidence record: harness/channel, binary version and path, source tag/commit where known, cwd and state-home identity, requested model/profile/CLI overrides, trusted layers and managed requirements, operation, supported/disabled/unknown, evidence kind, receipt and timestamp. Redact secrets; distinguish configuration evidence, available-tool evidence and demonstrated execution. A model catalog or version alone never proves all three.

Transport and background execution: test before replacement

The app-server protocol offers initialized connections, thread identity, typed items and turn completion statuses. turn/start acknowledgement, turn/started, completed items and turn/completed are different observations. turn/steer targets an expected active turn; it does not create a new turn. thread/inject_items persists history without starting a turn. Experimental thread read state is not a Cassy delivery ACK.

Cassy's current ui/factory/daemon/runtime/queue_and_events.rs:3051 distinguishes normal delivery turn evidence from byte submission; delivery_probe_jobs.rs:97, mux pane completion and commander_mirror.rs:166 already carry transport ownership. Route an experimental adapter through these seams instead of adding a second queue owner. Test UUID-targeted codex queue, reconnect/duplicate delivery, idle/busy states, turn attribution and failure controls with cas-353b. Queue acceptance alone cannot prove model consumption.

There is material counter-evidence to immediate replacement. The command reference calls app-server a development/debug surface that may change; the removed Codex MCP-server guide points at app-server while warning about experimental/production support. WebSocket transport is experimental. Use a private, version-pinned pilot with the existing PTY path retained. This task executed neither app-server nor queue delivery.

Do not confuse removal of Codex's own MCP-server mode with support for external MCP servers: Cassy's canonical cs stdio server is a Codex client integration. Keep mcp__cs__ naming/policy identity in crates/cas-mux/src/backend/codex.rs and PTY launch identity in crates/cas-pty/src/pty.rs:1473. CodeMode/ranked tool search and native alias changes require execution-level policy tests before changing exposure.

Background/process APIs have separate scope and maturity. Some app-server command-execution methods run outside the agent sandbox; they are not interchangeable with policy-governed model tool calls. Experimental terminal list/terminate/clean operations require exact owned process identity. Releases improve permission retention, cancellation and late-output draining, but Cassy's complete saved conformance pin is still crates/cas-pty/conformance/codex-cli-0.156.0-2026-09-23.json. Reuse d0fe's narrow 0.163 receipts without presenting them as a complete replacement conformance run.

State, compaction, account and profile boundaries

Configuration precedence layers explicit CLI, trusted project context, selected profile, user/cloud/system settings and defaults under managed constraints. Standalone named profile files replace removed legacy inline profiles; this is not a new 0.163 migration. Project config cannot redirect all sensitive provider/authentication settings. The beta permission profile system has compatibility/precedence rules with older sandbox flags and requires an active proxy for domain restrictions. Do not switch Cassy's launch policy during this research task.

Authentication storage can be file, keyring, automatic or ephemeral. cas-cli/src/accounts.rs:118 shares AGENTS, agents, hooks, config, plugins, skills and memories across account homes, while current account handling also reads auth.json. A distinct home directory is not sufficient proof of effective authenticated account when keyring or workspace constraints apply. Test identity/credential storage and shared-trust effects in a separately approved isolated fixture; this static review establishes a compatibility question, not a reproduced account leak.

Environment controls separate CODEX_HOME from SQLite home overrides. The shell environment policy applies filters and explicit sets in an order that can reintroduce excluded values; default secret exclusion must not be assumed. A future evidence harness should preserve required CAS authority markers while giving HOME/XDG/runtime/temp and Git state private roots and an explicit credential-free allowlist.

Native memories are optional, generated background context under Codex state. They do not replace Cassy's durable tasks/memory or authorize a second work owner. Manual compaction acknowledgement is distinct from a completed context-compaction item. Prefer documented item events over transcript-path scraping; a transcript path is not a stable API. Defer automatic/speculative compaction enablement and native goal continuation until cancellation, authority and context preservation are demonstrated. No memory/compaction performance benefit was measured here.

Codex-managed worktrees have their own storage/cleanup rules, and ignored-file copying is explicitly scoped to desktop-managed worktrees. Preserve Cassy's branch/worktree/scratch ownership; do not import desktop cleanup or secret-copy behavior into factory worktrees. New models/providers, Daybreak eligibility, cloud/plugin workflows and UI controls remain optional context rather than reasons to change account or execution policy.

Confidence, counter-evidence and implications

High confidence: published stable/tag provenance; the seven-release inventory; supported documented role/hook/config shapes; pinned V2 precedence; peer canary observations within their exact controls. Moderate confidence: which adapter will improve Cassy's delivery reliability, because no end-to-end transport comparison was run. Unknown: full effective native tools/roles for every model/profile, complete hook enforcement, account isolation across credential backends and any performance gain.

The strongest case against native adoption is support and authority mismatch: app-server support is limited, hook execution can fail open, roles inherit constraints and do not register independent reviewers, and current Cassy conformance is older. These are reasons for small reversible adapters with independent receipts. A supported native catalog/availability API or a production-support commitment could change the transport recommendation; failed real denial/continuation tests would narrow the lifecycle recommendation.

Send this matrix to cas-d0fe, cas-6c54 and cas-558a; pair it with cas-f1ca's Claude review. The common structure should keep one canonical Cassy role/policy source, harness-native projections, contextual evidence records and a transport adapter that preserves existing task/receipt ownership. Proposed tests without an assigned owner remain proposals, not newly authorized work. No runtime setting, verifier skip, trust bypass, model change or release gate follows automatically from this report.
